ai.title: Add openroutergpt5chat constant and tweak Peter Plan prompt
ai.summary: Added `openrouter_gpt5_chat` mapping to `openai/gpt-5-chat` in `common/src/constants.ts`. Updated `planner-factory.ts` spawner prompt for 'Peter Plan' to recommend usage for complex tasks requiring thinking, softening previous discouragement. Changes affect core model registry and agent planning behavior.

eli5.text: The assistant named Peter Plan now gets a gentler recommendation when deciding whether to use it for tricky tasks, so you're nudged to pick it for complex work that needs deep thinking rather than being told to avoid it. The system also learned about a new model option, GPT-5 Chat, adding it to the list of available assistants you can choose from. If you looked at the settings today, you'd see GPT-5 Chat listed alongside the other model names, and the guidance for when Peter Plan is most useful would read slightly less discouraging.

ai.title: Tool call timeouts resolve error result instead of rejecting
ai.summary: Timeouts in `requestToolCall` resolve with `{ success: false, error: ... }` instead of rejecting. Prevents agent crashes on tool timeouts. Scope: `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`.

eli5.text: If a tool call in the system times out, it now returns a failed result instead of crashing the assistant. You, as a user, would notice that the assistant keeps running and responds with an error message rather than stopping or freezing when a tool takes too long. This is a behind-the-scenes fix that prevents the assistant from breaking when tools don't respond quickly.

ai.title: Evals migrate to Codebuff SDK for prompting
ai.summary: Git evals replace direct `promptAiSdkStructured` calls with `CodebuffClient` via new `prompting-agent.ts`. This aligns evaluation harnesses with production SDK paths. Changes affect `evals/git-evals/` and `sdk/src/client.ts` (renamed `promptIdValues` to `promptIdToHandlers`).

eli5.text: If you run the automated tests that check how the assistant behaves, those tests now talk to the assistant through the same connection method a real program uses, rather than a separate shortcut built just for testing. In practice, you would not see a different conversation or a different answer, but if something fails to output anything, a new debug print will help figure out why. The change only touches the test and evaluation setup, so nothing a regular user does with the assistant is affected. It is live today for whoever runs those evaluations.

ai.title: Refine base2 agent prompts and spawnable agents
ai.summary: Updated system and instructions prompts for base2 agents (Buffy, editor) to include core mandates like proactiveness, clarity, and strict convention adherence. Expanded editor's spawnableAgents to include 'web-researcher' and 'docs-researcher', replacing 'researcher'. Added explicit Git Changes context injection via PLACEHOLDER.GIT_CHANGES_PROMPT in Buffy's system prompt. Renamed 'Current Git Changes' to 'Git Changes' in backend prompt generation.

eli5.text: The automated assistants that help write code have been given clearer instructions to be proactive, stick to coding conventions, and explain their work in plain language. When one assistant needs to look up information online or in documentation, it can now call on more specialized helper tools instead of a general-purpose one. Additionally, the system now shows the most recent code changes made in Git to the assistant before it starts working, so it has fresh context. These refinements improve how the AI coding agents coordinate and operate, making their behavior more predictable and effective. This change is internal and already live.
